summary: LAS VEGAS, July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VenHub Global, Inc. (NASDAQ: VHUB) (“VenHub” or the “Company”), a leader in fully autonomous Smart Store technology, is aware of recent third-party publicity concerning its financial position and future prospects and is providing the following
body_text: LAS VEGAS, July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VenHub Global, Inc. (NASDAQ: VHUB) (“VenHub” or the “Company”), a leader in fully autonomous Smart Store technology, is aware of recent third-party publicity concerning its financial position and future prospects and is providing the following clarification for stockholders. All financial and liquidity information being referenced publicly is drawn directly from VenHub’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025. In that filing, the Company disclosed its revenue, net loss, balance sheet position, and the existence of substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern without additional capital. VenHub made these disclosures transparently and in accordance with applicable U.S. securities laws and reporting requirements. Shahan Ohanessian, CEO of VenHub stated: “As a public company focused on growth, we view these law-firm publicity releases as meritless and distracting. We have disclosed our financial position transparently, and our focus remains on execution, financing our growth strategy, and building long-term stockholder value.” As of the date of this release, VenHub is not aware of any investigation, enforcement action, or proceeding by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission or any other governmental authority related to its disclosures or business practices. VenHub operates a capital-intensive, high-growth model in autonomous and AI-driven retail and has consistently communicated that it will require additional financing to execute its strategy. The Company is actively assessing and pursuing a range of financing and strategic options to support its operations and long-term plans, while continuing to focus on operational execution and disciplined cost management. Investors are encouraged to rely on VenHub’s official filings with the SEC, together with its press releases and investor communications, for accurate and current information about the Company. VenHub’s SEC filing history includes its March 24, 2026 Form 10-K and subsequent 2026 filings, which remain the authoritative source for company disclosures. VenHub does not intend to comment further on third-party statements at this time. About VenHub VenHub designs and builds autonomous Smart Stores that operate 24/7 without on-site staff. Each store combines robotic automation, real-time inventory tracking, and mobile-based checkout to provide secure, convenient retail access. The company is headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada. title: Amazon CloudWatch announces coding agent insights
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon CloudWatch announces coding agent insights
body_text: Amazon CloudWatch announces the launch of coding agent insights, giving engineering leaders visibility into how AI coding tools are driving value across their organization. Coding Agent Insights integrates with Claude apps gateway for AWS to collect telemetry from Claude Code without additional instrumentation. Other supported coding agents include Codex and GitHub Copilot. As organizations scale AI coding agent adoption, they need to understand return on investment. Coding agent insights is built on OpenTelemetry metrics emitted by your coding agents and presents them alongside your existing CloudWatch operational data. This helps you answer questions like which teams would benefit from expanded access, where are agents accelerating delivery, and how can you right-size token budgets across departments. You can track spend trends, set proactive token billing alerts, correlate agent adoption with improvements in commit throughput and pull request velocity, or identify the models delivering the best cost-to-output ratio for your workloads. CloudWatch coding agent insights is available in all AWS commercial regions except Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain), and Israel (Tel Aviv). Configure your Claude apps gateway to emit telemetry to CloudWatch using the setup guide and view the Coding Agent Insights dashboard in the CloudWatch console. Standard CloudWatch OpenTelemetry metric ingestion pricing applies — see metrics pricing for details. To learn more, see the documentation .

title: SAP Completes Acquisition of Prior Labs
summary: SAP has completed the acquisition of Prior Labs, the pioneer of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs). Read the news.
body_text: WALLDORF — SAP SE (NYSE: SAP) today announced it has completed the acquisition of Prior Labs, the pioneer of Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs). The acquisition will accelerate SAP’s success in TFMs that started with SAP-RPT-1 and bring one of the world’s leading TFM research teams into the SAP family. Prior Labs will continue to operate as an independent entity, with SAP committing to investing more than €1 billion over the next four years to scale it into a globally leading frontier AI lab for the structured data that underpins the world’s businesses. title: Best CRM Portals for Operations, Customer Success, and IT Teams
summary: Introduction CRM portals give customers, partners, and vendors secure self-service access to the data and workflows that matter to them, without requiring your team to play middleman. Instead of fielding repetitive support requests or manually sharing project status updates, you expose the right slices of your CRM system through a
body_text: Introduction CRM portals give customers, partners, and vendors secure self-service access to the data and workflows that matter to them, without requiring your team to play middleman. Instead of fielding repetitive support requests or manually sharing project status updates, you expose the right slices of your CRM system through a branded, permission-controlled interface. In 2026, the expectation is clear: external users want 24/7 accessibility to customer information, order tracking, and support channels. CRM portals provide that access while automating manual admin work that otherwise eats into your team's capacity. They allow external users to interact with a company's CRM system on their own terms, which directly improves customer experience. This guide compares seven leading CRM portal solutions across security, integration, cost, and usability so operations, customer success, IT, and product teams can find the right fit for their specific needs. How We Chose the Best CRM Portals Every portal on this list was evaluated against practical criteria that matter when you're actually building and running a portal, not just buying one. Here's what we looked at: Security and compliance. Does the platform support SSO, SAML, role-based access controls, MFA, and audit logs? Role-based security ensures data privacy and controls access in CRM portals, which is non-negotiable for regulated industries. User provisioning. How easily can you invite, manage, and scale external users? Can you handle more users as the business grows without a painful migration? Data visibility controls. Can you restrict access at the row, column, and action level? Secure file sharing is a key feature that protects sensitive documents during exchange. Self-service workflows. Does the portal support automation, triggers, and conditional logic to reduce administrative tasks? Branding and custom domains. Customization options allow branding in CRM portals, which matters for client-facing experiences. Integration capabilities. CRM portals should integrate with other business tools for efficiency, whether that means databases, APIs, or SaaS apps. Operating cost. What does pricing look like at 100 users versus 10,000? Implementation complexity matters too. Analytics and notifications. Automated notifications keep clients informed, and built-in dashboards help you monitor portal actions and usage patterns. Best 7 CRM Portals for Secure Self-Service Access 1. Jet Admin Jet Admin is a no-code business app builder that lets you create custom customer portal experiences on top of your existing data. Rather than locking you into a single CRM vendor's ecosystem, it connects to databases, APIs, spreadsheets, and SaaS tools you already use. Why It Stands Out: You use drag-and-drop UI components to build your portal interface, then layer on enterprise-grade permissions and automation without writing code. Standalone portals like this offer more flexibility and customization options than built-in alternatives. Best For: Teams that need to connect data from multiple sources like Google Sheets, HubSpot, PostgreSQL, or Salesforce, and expose it through a unified, branded portal. Key Strengths: Role-based access down to rows, columns, and actions 50+ data source integrations including databases, REST/GraphQL APIs, and SaaS tools Branded experiences with custom domain, theming, and custom sign-in flows Workflow automation with triggers, conditions, and actions Set user authorization and access rights with granular control SSO/SAML, audit logs, and activity tracking Possible Limitations: Building a portal still requires configuration time, especially for complex relational data models. Pricing may scale with the number of external users and the complexity of your setup. 2. Salesforce Experience Cloud Salesforce Experience Cloud is the enterprise-grade portal platform built natively on top of Salesforce CRM. It supports customer, partner, and vendor portals with deep access to CRM objects. Why It Stands Out: If your entire organization already runs on Salesforce, Experience Cloud provides native integration with your sales pipeline, cases, and marketing data. CRM portals like this can boost sales by identifying customer buying patterns through shared analytics. Best For: Large enterprises with complex portal requirements, multiple user types, and existing Salesforce investments. Key Strengths: Native CRM integration with all Salesforce objects Advanced sharing rules and Apex-based visibility logic Lightning components for custom portal pages Mobile-optimized, responsive design Strong analytics via embedded reports and dashboards Possible Limitations: High licensing costs, especially for external user licenses. Implementation often requires specialized Salesforce developers or consulting partners. Total cost of ownership can be 3–5× the initial subscription. 3. Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Portal Microsoft Dynamics 365 offers portal capabilities through Power Apps Portals, tightly integrated with the Dynamics 365 CRM and the broader Microsoft ecosystem. Why It Stands Out: CRM portals built here facilitate better collaboration between internal and external teams thanks to seamless integration with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Azure AD. Best For: Organizations already invested in Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 seeking unified identity management and familiar interfaces. Key Strengths: Deep integration with Azure AD for SSO and identity management Power BI analytics embedded in portal views Multilingual support and custom domain capabilities Enhanced security through Microsoft's compliance framework Possible Limitations: Steep learning curve for portal configuration. Limited flexibility if you need to connect non-Microsoft data sources. External user licensing adds cost on top of existing Dynamics 365 subscriptions. 4. HubSpot Service Hub HubSpot's Service Hub includes a customer portal focused on support and self-service, integrated with HubSpot's CRM and marketing automation tools. Why It Stands Out: Customers can independently track orders and manage accounts through a CRM portal, submit support requests online, and access a knowledge base. Self-service features reduce the need for in-person assistance. Best For: Growing businesses that prioritize customer support alongside marketing automation without heavy technical investment. Key Strengths: Easy setup with minimal technical resources Integrated ticketing and shared inbox Knowledge base and community features built in Reasonable pricing for small to mid-sized teams Possible Limitations: Limited ability to expose transactional CRM modules (custom objects, quotes, invoices) to external users. Basic role controls compared to enterprise solutions. Costs escalate on higher tiers when you need more features. 5. Zoho CRM Plus Zoho CRM offers mature portal functionality supporting customers, partners, vendors, and franchise networks. You define primary and related modules, then control what external users can view, edit, or delete. Why It Stands Out: Personalization options enhance the customer portal experience, and Zoho's ecosystem provides access to 40+ integrated apps across sales, support, and marketing. Best For: Small to medium businesses needing flexible portal configurations at competitive pricing. First 1,000 portal users are free, with tiered pricing beyond that. Key Strengths: Multi-portal support for different user groups Field-level permissions and record-level visibility controls Affordable pricing (1,001–2,000 users at ~$3/user/month) GDPR compliance features including data subject rights Possible Limitations: Interface complexity increases with module relationships. SMS-based portal invitations are region-limited. Cost can reach ~$9,000/month at 5,000 external users depending on tier. 6. Zendesk Zendesk provides a customer portal centered on support and community engagement, with a strong knowledge base and self-service tools. Why It Stands Out: Customer self-service portals enhance customer experience and satisfaction. Organizations using CRM portals like Zendesk can see improved customer satisfaction and loyalty through community features and streamlined support. Best For: Support teams that want to simplify communication with customers through community forums and ai tools for automated responses. Key Strengths: Community forums and discussion features Tight support ticket integration Mobile-friendly portal design Good analytics on support metrics and CSAT Possible Limitations: Limited to support use cases. Not designed for exposing transactional CRM data like deals, invoices, or supply chain management records. Basic data integration with external databases. 7. Freshworks Customer Portal Freshworks offers a customer portal through Freshdesk that combines self-service, knowledge base, and community features under a user friendly interface. Why It Stands Out: User-friendly interfaces enhance the effectiveness of CRM portals. Freshworks portals streamline support and ticketing processes for clients, and their Freddy AI bot has helped companies like PhonePe resolve ~80% of support tickets automatically . Best For: Teams seeking a balance between simplicity and functionality for customer portals, especially for multi-brand support. Key Strengths: Intuitive, WCAG-compliant portal design Multiple portals for different products from one instance Automation features including AI-powered responses Multilingual support and SSO Possible Limitations: Less capable for exposing transactional CRM data beyond support tickets. Deep customization may require higher-tier plans. Limited enterprise-scale features for partner or vendor portals. Quick Comparison of the Best CRM Portals CRM portals come in standalone and built-in types. Standalone portals like Jet Admin offer more flexibility and customization options, while built-in portals like HubSpot's are simpler to set up and user friendly. Here's how they compare: Solution Best For Portal Type External User Pricing Key Differentiator Jet Admin Custom portals on existing data Standalone Scales with usage Multi-source data connections Salesforce Experience Cloud Enterprise-scale portals Built-in Per-user license (premium) Native Salesforce CRM integration Microsoft Dynamics 365 Microsoft ecosystem orgs Built-in Add-on licensing Azure AD + Power BI integration HubSpot Service Hub Support + marketing Built-in Included in tiers Easy setup, marketing alignment Zoho CRM Plus Affordable flexibility Built-in First 1K free, then tiered Zoho's ecosystem of 40+ apps Zendesk Support communities Built-in Plan-based Community forums + AI Freshworks Simple multi-brand portals Built-in Plan-based Freddy AI, WCAG compliance How to Choose the Right CRM Portal Selecting the right CRM portal software starts with understanding three fundamental dimensions: your data, your security posture, and your users' expectations. Define the purpose and features of your CRM portal before evaluating vendors. Choose Based on Your Data Architecture If your customer data lives across multiple databases, APIs, and SaaS apps, you need a portal that can connect to all of them without forcing a migration. Client portal software like Jet Admin connects directly to PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce, HubSpot, and dozens of other tools. If everything lives inside one CRM system, a built-in portal from that vendor may be simpler. Consider whether you need to track leads, manage a sales pipeline, or handle file sharing alongside support, as each use case demands different data integrations. Choose Based on Security Requirements External-user security is where portals either earn trust or create risk. Enhanced security through SSO/SAML, MFA, and audit logs is essential. Secure file exchange ensures data integrity and confidentiality across client interaction touchpoints. Look for row-level and field-level access controls to prevent data breaches, especially if partners or vendors need easy access to sensitive records. For regulated industries, ensure the portal supports GDPR and CCPA compliance features, including consent management and data subject rights. Choose Based on User Experience Needs Client portals provide collaborative workspaces for clients and businesses when they are well-designed. Look for solutions that support custom domains, responsive design, and branding that matches your company identity. Customers who can stay organized within a clean, mobile-friendly portal are far more likely to adopt self-service over email or phone. Ensure your CRM portal is scalable to accommodate business growth, so the experience doesn't degrade as you add more users. Which Option Is Best for You? Choose Jet Admin if you need to easily manage portal experiences across multiple data sources, want granular permissions, and prefer building on your existing databases and APIs rather than migrating to a new CRM. Choose Salesforce Experience Cloud if you require enterprise-scale portal capabilities and your entire organization already depends on Salesforce for a complete view of customer interactions. Choose Microsoft Dynamics 365 if you're invested in the Microsoft stack and want a portal that works across Dynamics 365, Office 365, and Azure without friction across time zone boundaries. Choose HubSpot Service Hub if you prioritize integrated customer support features alongside marketing and want a portal that helps you make smarter decisions about follow ups and communication. Choose Zoho CRM Plus if you need comprehensive portal functionality at competitive pricing. Zoho CRM handles everything from task management to support within a single, interconnected software platform. Choose Zendesk if community building and support are your primary requirements and other tools in your stack handle the transactional CRM work. Choose Freshworks if you want a user friendly interface for customer portal software without the complexity of enterprise platforms, especially for a tech company or software company scaling support operations. Final Thoughts The best CRM portal is the one that fits your data architecture, meets your security standards, and delivers self service portals your external users will actually adopt. Customer portals can increase customer satisfaction and loyalty when they provide 24/7 access to customer information, support, and collaboration tools. They also help teams stay organized and let the entire organization benefit from reduced manual workload. Start with your core requirements: what data do you need to expose, who needs access, and what level of customization and branding matters? As your business grows, expand from there. If you need a configurable portal that connects to your existing databases and apps, explore Jet Admin's portal builder to see how it works with your data.

title: How McDermott Cut $1.4M in Hiring Costs With Live Visibility
summary: Without live equipment visibility, McDermott leaned on outside hiring to cover the gap. See how real-time monitoring eliminated $1.4M in costs.
body_text: TL;DR: One-Minute Brief When a large yard and marine operation has no live way to see what its equipment is actually doing, the default fix is more people, extra supervisors and inspectors brought on to cover the visibility gap manually. This is the story of how McDermott closed that gap with real-time, AI-driven equipment monitoring instead, eliminating 1.4 million dollars in outside hiring costs while cutting downtime by 27 percent and lifting productivity and safety at the same time. The Problem: Paying People to Compensate for a Visibility Gap Running a large-scale yard and marine operation means keeping track of a wide mix of equipment across a sprawling site, in McDermott’s case, more than a thousand yard and barge assets moving through the same operation. Without a live, automated way to see what every piece of equipment was actually doing at any given moment, the practical answer to that visibility problem was headcount: bringing on additional outside supervisors and inspectors whose job was essentially to be extra eyes on the yard, manually checking on equipment status, utilization, and safety conditions that a system should have been able to report automatically. That approach worked, in the sense that it got the visibility McDermott needed, but it was an expensive way to solve what was fundamentally a data problem with a headcount solution. Every additional supervisor or inspector brought on to cover the gap was a recurring cost that would keep accumulating for as long as the underlying visibility problem remained unsolved, rather than a one-time fix. The Approach: Real-Time, AI-Driven Equipment Monitoring McDermott’s move was to replace that manual oversight layer with a system built to provide the same visibility automatically. AI-driven monitoring across the equipment fleet gave the operation a live, continuous view of what machines were doing, working, idling, or flagged for attention, without needing a person physically watching each one. That same real-time visibility extended into safety monitoring, giving the team automated awareness of conditions that previously required manual inspection to catch. The shift wasn’t about adding another layer on top of the existing manual process. It was about removing the need for that manual layer entirely, letting the system provide the continuous coverage that used to require additional outside hires to deliver. The Result: $1.4M in Costs Eliminated, 27% Less Downtime The most direct result was financial: real-time visibility eliminated the need for the outside hiring that had been covering the gap, removing 1.4 million dollars in associated costs. That number reflects a recurring cost that stopped needing to recur, not a one-time saving, since the supervisory and inspection headcount that visibility gap used to require was no longer necessary once the system could provide the same coverage automatically. Alongside that, AI-driven equipment monitoring boosted productivity and safety across the operation while cutting downtime by 27 percent. Reduced downtime in particular reflects what continuous visibility makes possible that manual, periodic inspection cannot: catching equipment issues and unsafe conditions closer to the moment they start, rather than at whatever interval a human inspection cycle happened to allow. What This Case Shows About the Cost of Manual Visibility McDermott’s experience is a clear example of a pattern that shows up across large, equipment-heavy operations: when there’s no automated way to see what’s happening across a fleet, the gap gets filled with people, and that solution scales in cost exactly as fast as the operation grows. A visibility problem solved with headcount keeps costing more as the fleet expands, while a visibility problem solved with real-time monitoring scales without that same growing cost, and, in McDermott’s case, delivered a meaningful downtime reduction on top of the direct cost savings. How Tenderd Helped McDermott Get There Tenderd’s real-time, AI-driven equipment monitoring gave McDermott continuous visibility across a yard and marine operation of more than a thousand assets, without relying on additional outside supervisors and inspectors to cover the gap manually. That shift eliminated 1.4 million dollars in outside hiring costs while cutting downtime by 27 percent and improving productivity and safety across the operation. The Bottom Line When a fleet has no automated way to see what’s happening, the visibility gap gets filled with people, and that fix gets more expensive as the operation grows. McDermott’s results show what happens when that gap gets closed with real-time monitoring instead: a large, recurring cost eliminated, and a meaningful drop in downtime as a direct result of catching issues earlier. Want to see what replacing manual oversight with real-time visibility could look like for your own operation? Get in touch with the Tenderd team for a walkthrough: Book a Demo Frequently Asked Questions Why was McDermott spending on outside hiring in the first place? Without a live, automated way to monitor equipment status, utilization, and safety conditions across a large yard and marine operation, additional outside supervisors and inspectors were brought on to cover that visibility gap manually. How did real-time monitoring eliminate that hiring cost specifically? Once AI-driven monitoring could automatically provide the equipment and safety visibility that outside hires had been manually covering, the recurring need for that additional headcount went away, along with its associated cost. What caused the 27 percent reduction in downtime? Continuous, real-time monitoring catches equipment issues closer to the moment they start, rather than only at whatever interval a periodic manual inspection allowed, which is what drives a meaningful reduction in downtime. Does this kind of visibility gap only affect large operations? The pattern shows up wherever manual oversight is being used to compensate for a lack of automated visibility, but it becomes more expensive as an operation scales, since headcount-based coverage keeps costing more as the fleet grows. Is cost savings the only benefit of this kind of monitoring? No. In McDermott's case, the same real-time monitoring that eliminated outside hiring costs also improved productivity and safety, showing that the visibility gap being solved had implications well beyond headcount spend alone.

title: How to get 2 phone numbers on 1 phone in minutes

body_text: Your personal phone number has become your business line, and it’s starting to show. Clients text you after hours, and you hesitate before answering calls from numbers you don’t recognize. You’re always “on,” even when you’re off the clock. That’s why you’re wondering if you can have two phone numbers on one phone. Luckily, it’s possible — and the process is simpler than you might think. You don’t need an extra cell phone or a device with a dual SIM card to get another phone number. You just need the right virtual phone provider. We’ll guide you through the three simple steps to get a second phone number on your current mobile device, whether you’re looking for a second phone number for iPhone or Android. Then, we’ll dive deeper into how your second number will work. Can you have 2 phone numbers on one phone? Yes, with most Voice over Internet Protocol or VoIP systems , you can set up more than two phone numbers on one phone. VoIP solutions like Quo, formerly OpenPhone, let you add multiple numbers to your existing device without the need for a second SIM card or a dual-SIM phone. This feature is useful for separating your personal and business communications. Quo offers iOS and Android apps that your team can use to access your business phone numbers . Make and receive phone calls, send text messages, and work with your team on a simple platform that helps you grow your customer interactions. If you need to multitask when you’re in the office, you can use our Mac, Windows, and browser apps to get more work done while you’re on the phone. Want to let your customers know when you’re calling them? Assign a business caller ID to each of your phone numbers in your Quo account settings. Your customers are more likely to have confidence in who’s calling them instead of worrying about spam or robocallers dialing their number. Compare this easy, flexible option to purchasing a traditional landline or physical dual SIM phone, which is a type of device that can also support two numbers. Unlike VoIP phones , phones with dual SIM cards limit you to two numbers only, and you typically need to buy separate plans from your carrier for each. 3 Ways to get a second phone number on your phone If you’re looking to get a second phone number on your device, you have a few options. 1. Dual SIM phones A dual SIM phone has two SIM card slots or supports one physical SIM card and one eSIM, allowing you to use two phone numbers on one phone. This is a good option if you only want two personal phone numbers and don’t need access to business features. 2. Carrier add-on services Some mobile carriers let you add an alternate phone number for an additional monthly fee. These services typically include basic calling and texting, but they don’t offer any way to save time catching up on conversations or automating phone-related tasks. 3. VoIP apps VoIP apps like Quo let you add multiple business phone numbers to the device you already own. They’re a good fit if you want more than basic calling and texting. You can share numbers with teammates, route calls during business hours, and connect your phone system to your CRM. How to get 2 phone numbers on one phone in 3 steps Get two phone numbers on one phone in minutes by signing up for a VoIP service like Quo. This allows you to access a VoIP phone number , which you can use to make and receive calls using an app on your mobile phone and computer. Here’s how you can get two phone numbers on one phone with Quo: Get a second phone number in minutes Try for free 1. Create a Quo account Start a free seven-day trial and confirm that Quo is a great fit for you. Verify your account with an existing phone number and your credit card information. Your card won’t be charged until the trial ends, and you can cancel at any time. We’ll even send you a heads up via email in case you change your mind. See how easy it is to create an account below: 2. Pick your phone number We’ll automatically suggest a new number, but you can also choose from any available local US, Canadian , or North American toll-free number . Want to move an existing phone number to Quo? You can port a number right from the web or mobile app. 3. Download the mobile app Head to the App Store for iOS or Google Play Store for Android to download the Quo app on your phone. Once you’re in, you can start using a new business line without needing a different phone. Even after you add a business line to your cell phone , your personal phone number will still be tied to your device. Your business number will be connected to your VoIP account and WiFi, so you won’t incur extra charges from your carrier. 6 Reasons why you may need two phone numbers on one phone Still considering why you need two phone numbers on one phone? Having multiple numbers on one device makes it easier to manage your personal and work communications simultaneously. It also offers multiple additional benefits if you’re managing a growing business: 1. You don’t want to carry another phone Carrying a separate phone for work is just plain annoying. It turns into one more thing to charge, keep track of, and lug around. With a second number on a single device, you get all the benefits of two lines without the extra bulk. With a business phone system like Quo, you can also implement a Bring Your Own Device or BYOD policy . This lets your team use their preferred devices for work. You can assign each team member a dedicated phone number without having to purchase physical SIM cards. 2. You need to separate personal and business calls With a VoIP system, you can clearly see when an incoming call is coming to your work phone number. This helps you answer professionally when calls are for business. Quo will display text that says “Quo Audio” alongside the Quo app icon for your VoIP calls. If you have multiple phone numbers in your Quo account, you can also add a name and emoji to each inbox. That way, you can easily keep on top of which number your callers are attempting to reach. 3. You need to maintain a better work-life balance As you may have experienced yourself, it gets more difficult to have work-life balance if your customers call your personal phone number outside of business hours. A second number lets you set clear boundaries so you can unplug and take personal calls without worrying about missing important work calls. Plus, you can route calls based on your availability. Set up business hours call routing so you can take calls during working hours and route them after hours. Direct calls to our backup call forwarding options, including an AI answering service , custom voicemail, and SMS auto-replies. 4. You need to prioritize security Sharing your personal mobile number for business can expose you to unwanted calls, spam, or security risks. A second number helps protect your privacy and keeps sensitive business communication separate from your personal life. 5. You need business continuity When your business number doubles as your personal number, there’s no backup plan. If you’re unavailable, calls go unanswered. There’s no call routing, no shared inbox, and no way for a teammate to step in. A second business number can give your team access to shared calling and messaging, so conversations don’t stop when one person can’t answer the phone. 6. You need to access complete conversation history Quo keeps all customer communication in one place with a dedicated business number. Call transcripts and AI-generated call summaries with next steps make it easy to review conversations and follow up effectively. See how OnCentive uses Quo to give every teammate visibility into customer conversations. VoIP vs dual SIM phones: What’s better? If you’re looking for ways to add another number to your phone, you have two options: VoIP phones and dual SIM phones. title: Increases in HbA1c Testing Follow Expanded Medicare Screening Coverage
summary: Quest Diagnostics presented research results at the American Diabetes Association’s 2026 Scientific Sessions, which occurred in New Orleans on June 5-8. The study, presented as a poster, was...
body_text: Quest Diagnostics presented research results at the American Diabetes Association’s 2026 Scientific Sessions, which occurred in New Orleans on June 5-8. The study, presented as a poster, was titled “ Increases in Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) Testing Following Expanded Medicare Screening Coverage .” The researchers, which included a diabetes expert from the University of Pittsburgh, shared insights into increases in glycated hemoglobin (hbA1c) testing following expanded Medicare screening coverage for the test. Prior to 2024, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) coverage for diabetes screening was limited to fasting glucose and an oral glucose tolerance test, both of which have disadvantages. Fasting glucose measurement can be problematic because some patients with impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes may have glucose levels within the reference range at the time of the measurement. And, for some patients, traditional oral glucose tolerance tests can be too time and labor intensive. On January 1, 2024, CMS expanded coverage to include use of hbA1c tests for diabetic screening. To measure the impact of the expansion, the study analyzed hbA1c testing patterns between two periods: January 1, 2022 through September 30, 2022 (“Period 1”) and January 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025 (“Period 2”), performed by Quest on patients >65 years without any prior diagnosis of type 1 diabetes (T1D) or type 2 diabetes (T2D). There was a statistically significant increase of 30.1% in mean monthly testing volume between Period 1 and Period 2 (p < 0.0001). This increase may indicate that clinicians were aware of the Medicare policy change noted above. Another notable finding was an increase in the percentage of patients who tested positive for prediabetes (defined as HbA1c 5.7-6.4%) from 37% in period 1 to 55% in period 2. The study’s strengths included the large volume of testing from a national diagnostic laboratory in both periods. Limitations were a lack of clinical data and, as such, an inability to confirm whether positive screens led to confirmatory testing or initiation of therapy. In closing, these findings suggest that the Medicare policy change, along with the demonstrated increase in hbA1c testing for diabetes screening, may help inform those 65 years of age and older of a new diagnosis of prediabetes. Approximately 500,000 to 600,000 new cases of diabetes occur every year within this age group. With knowledge of a prediabetes diagnosis, earlier intervention may be possible to prevent disease progression and complications – empowering more patients with insights to make health proactive, connected, and personal.
